marketMacroRotation.verdict: Accelerator spend still leads; the emerging rotation signal is broader AI infrastructure - CPUs, servers, memory, networking, power, and ROI discipline.
marketMacroRotation.status: Broadening beyond accelerators, not a single-lane rotation

lanes.name: Accelerators still lead
items: NVIDIA data-center revenue remains the cleanest AI spend read-through, with Q4 FY2026 data-center revenue up 75% year over year.
AMD's data-center growth is still a combined EPYC CPU and Instinct GPU story, not a pure CPU shift.
Hyperscaler capex is still rising, and much of the budget remains tied to accelerators, memory, networking, and full rack systems.

lanes.name: AI stack broadening
items: Agentic AI and inference workloads need more orchestration, scheduling, tool execution, memory movement, storage, networking, and general-purpose compute.
NVIDIA Vera, Arm AGI CPU, AMD EPYC demand, Intel Xeon commentary, memory pricing, and hyperscaler capex all point to a wider AI infrastructure trade.
Server OEMs, rack builders, power suppliers, cooling vendors, and data-center operators become more important if buyers move from scarce chips to complete AI factories.

lanes.name: Confirmation needed
items: Watch whether non-accelerator AI infrastructure revisions accelerate faster than accelerator/HBM revisions over the next two earnings cycles.
Confirm that CPU, memory, networking, storage, power, and cooling demand shows up in deployed systems, not only vendor product launches.
Treat any single-subtheme slowdown as a separate signal; the current evidence says broadening, not a simple leadership handoff.

demandChain.title: If AI demand keeps rising, what gets pulled next?
demandChain.summary: The AI buildout works like a chain: more users and agents create more tokens; tokens need accelerators; accelerators need memory, CPUs, networking, storage, power, cooling, and cash-flow discipline. The next shortage is usually where demand is high but capacity takes longer to add.

position.nowSummary: CPU/server demand and networking/optics are the active rotation zone after the accelerator and memory move.
position.nextSummary: Power, cooling, grid interconnects, and electrical delivery look like the next physical cap if AI demand keeps compounding. Step 6 potential is now led by POWL, MOD, IESC, BE, AAON, and STRL, with POWL the closest AMD-like bottleneck setup.

stages.name: AI usage and agents
stages.need: More paid usage, longer context, tool calls, inference latency, and enterprise workloads.
stages.nextWatch: AI revenue run-rate, paid seats, token volume, enterprise conversion, and whether software pricing sticks.

stages.name: Accelerators
stages.need: GPU, ASIC, TPU, and accelerator capacity for training and inference.
stages.nextWatch: NVIDIA data-center growth, AMD Instinct ramp, custom silicon orders, HBM attach, and gross margins.

stages.name: Memory and SSDs
stages.need: HBM for accelerators, DDR5 for inference servers, and enterprise SSDs for data-heavy workloads.
stages.nextWatch: HBM4 validation, DDR5 contract prices, NAND/enterprise SSD pricing, and whether memory costs squeeze device makers.

stages.name: CPU and servers
stages.need: General compute for orchestration, inference serving, data prep, scheduling, security, and rack-level systems.
stages.nextWatch: EPYC/Xeon demand, Arm server traction, AI server attach ratios, and traditional server refresh.

stages.name: Networking and optics
stages.need: 800G/1.6T optics, Ethernet/InfiniBand fabric, retimers, switches, and optical circuit switching.
stages.nextWatch: 800G and 1.6T shipment growth, switch silicon, optical module lead times, and cluster utilization.

stages.name: Power, cooling, and grid
stages.need: Megawatts, interconnects, transformers, switchgear, UPS, liquid cooling, and data-center thermal capacity.
stages.nextWatch: Grid queues, transformer lead times, data-center power availability, liquid-cooling orders, and utility rate pushback.

stages.name: ROI and free cash flow
stages.need: Cloud revenue, utilization, AI product pricing, and free cash flow after capex.
stages.nextWatch: Capex-to-revenue conversion, cloud margins, customer ROI proof, and whether AI spend becomes paid usage.

bottleneckCandidates.name: Power, grid interconnects, and transformers
bottleneckCandidates.why: Data centers can be planned faster than grids can be upgraded. IEA says grid queues are at record levels, with more than 2,500 GW of generation, storage, and large-load projects stalled worldwide.
bottleneckCandidates.watch: Transformer/switchgear lead times, grid connection queues, utility capex, on-site generation, and power availability by data-center market.

bottleneckCandidates.name: Cooling and rack power density
bottleneckCandidates.why: Higher-density AI racks turn compute into a heat-removal and power-delivery problem. Liquid cooling, UPS, busways, enclosures, and commissioning skill become gating items.
bottleneckCandidates.watch: Liquid-cooling backlog, rack power density, data-center thermal orders, and whether servers ship but cannot be deployed at full density.
bottleneckCandidates.source: Uptime Institute 2026 predictions / IEA Energy and AI update

bottleneckCandidates.name: Memory wall: HBM, DDR5, and enterprise SSDs
bottleneckCandidates.why: TrendForce says AI server demand is driving sharp DRAM and NAND contract price increases as suppliers reallocate capacity toward HBM, server DRAM, and enterprise SSDs.
bottleneckCandidates.watch: HBM4 qualification, server DDR5 pricing, NAND contract prices, enterprise SSD demand, and memory cost pressure in PCs/phones.
bottleneckCandidates.source: TrendForce memory pricing and HBM reports

bottleneckCandidates.name: Networking, optics, and data movement
bottleneckCandidates.why: Larger AI clusters need faster scale-out networks. LightCounting expects 800G shipments to more than double in 2026 and 1.6T ports to grow from a small base to tens of millions.
bottleneckCandidates.watch: 800G/1.6T optics, switch silicon, optical circuit switching, retimers, and customer concentration at hyperscalers.
bottleneckCandidates.source: LightCounting / Arista Q1 2026 / Cisco Silicon One G300

bottleneckCandidates.name: Storage and data layer
bottleneckCandidates.why: Production AI needs retrieval, vector search, checkpoints, logs, training data, and fast inference data paths. If GPU clusters wait on data, compute utilization falls.
bottleneckCandidates.watch: Enterprise SSD orders, object storage growth, vector database adoption, cloud storage growth, and data platform consumption.
bottleneckCandidates.source: TrendForce NAND/enterprise SSD commentary and AI data platform earnings read-throughs

bottleneckCandidates.name: Advanced packaging, test, and yield control
bottleneckCandidates.why: HBM, chiplets, retimers, and advanced AI packages need more CoWoS-style packaging, inspection, metrology, and high-power test intensity.
bottleneckCandidates.watch: TSMC advanced packaging capex, HBM packaging capacity, semicap orders, AI test intensity, and yield commentary.
bottleneckCandidates.source: Semicap and test company earnings read-throughs

evidence.headline: Data-center cooling demand accelerated
evidence.detail: Modine reported Q3 FY2026 data-center sales up 78% year over year and raised its data-center growth outlook to more than 70% for the year.

evidence.headline: Data-center revenue stayed at record scale
evidence.detail: Q4 FY2026 data-center revenue was $62.3B, up 75% year over year; FY2026 data-center revenue was $193.7B, up 68%. This is the main counter-evidence against declaring the accelerator cycle over.

evidence.headline: NVIDIA made CPU a first-class AI factory product
evidence.detail: Vera CPU was positioned for data processing, AI training, and agentic inference, with cloud and system partners including Meta, Oracle Cloud, Dell, HPE, Lenovo, and Supermicro.

evidence.headline: Arm moved from IP into data-center CPU silicon
evidence.detail: Arm introduced an Arm-designed data-center CPU for agentic AI infrastructure, with Meta as lead partner and a message that CPUs coordinate distributed AI systems at scale.

evidence.headline: Oracle AI buildout pulled in behind-the-meter power
evidence.detail: Bloom and Oracle expanded their strategic partnership to support up to 2.8 GW of AI infrastructure power, with 1.2 GW initially contracted.

evidence.headline: Agentic AI is changing CPU:GPU ratios
evidence.detail: TrendForce argued that AI agents can raise CPU demand materially, citing a possible move toward 1:1 to 1:2 CPU-to-GPU ratios and higher CPU core demand per GW of AI infrastructure.

evidence.headline: Intel tied AI inference and agentic workloads to CPU demand
evidence.detail: Intel reported DCAI revenue of $5.1B, up 22% year over year, and highlighted Xeon 6 wins with Google workload-optimized instances and NVIDIA DGX Rubin NVL8 systems.

evidence.headline: MEP backlog nearly doubled
evidence.detail: Comfort Systems reported Q1 2026 backlog of $12.45B, up from $6.89B a year earlier, reinforcing strong demand for large complex facilities.

evidence.headline: AI revenue scaled, but infrastructure spend stayed heavy
evidence.detail: Microsoft said AI annual revenue run rate surpassed $37B, up 123% year over year, while Azure and other cloud services grew 40%. Cash paid for property and equipment was $30.9B in the quarter.

evidence.headline: Meta raised capex again for AI infrastructure
evidence.detail: Meta lifted 2026 capex guidance to $125B-$145B, citing higher component pricing and additional data-center costs to support future capacity.

evidence.headline: AWS growth remained strong while component risk persisted
evidence.detail: AWS Q1 2026 net sales were $37.6B, up 28% year over year. Amazon's outlook called out resource and supply volatility, including memory chips.

evidence.headline: Applied HVAC bookings surged
evidence.detail: Trane said Americas Commercial HVAC bookings rose about 40%, with applied equipment bookings up more than 160%, a useful read-through for data-center cooling demand.

evidence.headline: Switchgear demand showed up as a record data-center order
evidence.detail: Powell reported Q2 FY2026 orders up 97% year over year and disclosed a post-quarter data-center order above $400M, the largest in company history.

evidence.headline: AMD data-center growth included both EPYC CPUs and Instinct GPUs
evidence.detail: AMD reported Q1 revenue of $10.3B, up 38% year over year, and data-center revenue of $5.8B, up 57%, driven by EPYC processors and continued Instinct GPU ramp.

evidence.headline: Large-load requests kept rising
evidence.detail: AEP raised expected incremental large load to 63 GW by 2030 and lifted its capital plan, showing how data-center growth is feeding regulated grid investment.

metrics.watch: AMD Data Center mix, Intel DCAI growth, Arm royalty/server commentary, Dell and SMCI traditional server demand.

metrics.watch: NVIDIA data-center growth, AMD Instinct revenue, Blackwell/Rubin supply, HBM availability, and gross margins.

metrics.watch: Microsoft, Meta, Amazon, Alphabet, and Oracle capex, cloud growth, RPO/backlog, and AI revenue run-rate disclosure.

companyCandidates.name: Powell Industries
companyCandidates.why: Most direct untracked Step 6 electrical bottleneck name. Q2 FY2026 orders rose 97%, backlog reached $1.8B, and management disclosed a post-quarter data-center order above $400M tied to behind-the-meter on-site generation assets.
companyCandidates.risks: Large-project lumpiness, backlog conversion, margin normalization, execution risk, and remaining oil/gas cycle exposure.
companyCandidates.potentialRead: Closest Step 6 parallel to AMD: direct bottleneck exposure, a smaller revenue base, nearly doubled orders, no net debt pressure, and a single record data-center award large enough to reset expectations.

companyCandidates.name: Modine Manufacturing
companyCandidates.why: Clean cooling add. Modine said Q3 FY2026 data-center sales rose 78% year over year, lifted fiscal-year data-center growth outlook above 70%, and guided to 50%-70% annual data-center sales growth for the next two years.
companyCandidates.risks: Capacity ramp costs, debt/working capital, design shifts in cooling architecture, customer concentration, and valuation already pricing AI upside.
companyCandidates.potentialRead: Best clean cooling rerating candidate: data-center demand is already moving the revenue mix, and the legacy auto exit makes the AI cooling story easier for the market to underwrite.

companyCandidates.name: IES Holdings
companyCandidates.why: Data-center demand is explicitly driving Communications and Infrastructure Solutions growth. Fiscal Q2 2026 Communications revenue rose 35%, Infrastructure Solutions revenue rose 64%, and total backlog reached $3.86B.
companyCandidates.risks: Smaller/liquidity risk, residential segment drag, project concentration, labor execution, acquisition integration, and high expectations after a strong stock move.
companyCandidates.potentialRead: Strong AMD-like operating leverage because data centers are driving two high-growth segments, while its smaller scale and lower liquidity keep the rerating less fully institutionalized.

companyCandidates.name: Bloom Energy
companyCandidates.subTheme: On-site fuel-cell power for AI campuses
companyCandidates.why: Direct behind-the-meter power optionality. Bloom and Oracle expanded their partnership to support up to 2.8 GW of AI infrastructure power, including 1.2 GW initially contracted and deploying across Oracle US projects.
companyCandidates.risks: Very high valuation, customer concentration, manufacturing scale, fuel economics, and technology substitution.
companyCandidates.potentialRead: Most asymmetric Step 6 power name if behind-the-meter generation becomes a standard hyperscaler workaround, but valuation, customer concentration, and execution risk keep it below the top three.

companyCandidates.name: AAON
companyCandidates.why: Direct data-center cooling exposure through BASX and coil products. FY2025 results showed BASX sales up 138.8%, BASX backlog up 141.3%, total backlog up 110.9%, and liquid-cooling sales in AAON Coil Products up sharply.
companyCandidates.risks: ERP/ramp execution, new capacity costs, margin pressure, customer concentration, and cash needs while scaling data-center production.
companyCandidates.potentialRead: Direct liquid-cooling and custom air-side exposure with a real backlog step-up; the upside depends on clean execution as Memphis and Longview capacity ramp.

companyCandidates.name: Sterling Infrastructure
companyCandidates.why: Data centers are central to the E-Infrastructure growth story, and the CEC Facilities deal added mission-critical electrical and mechanical contracting. Q1 2026 revenue rose 92%, adjusted EPS rose 120%, and the company raised full-year guidance.
companyCandidates.risks: Construction-cycle exposure, acquisition integration, project margin risk, and valuation already reflecting fast data-center growth.
companyCandidates.potentialRead: Fastest visible construction-growth profile in the group after CEC, with strong data-center read-through; acquisition integration and post-earnings rerating temper the score.

companyCandidates.name: Comfort Systems USA
companyCandidates.why: Direct MEP contractor and modular fabrication beneficiary. Q1 2026 revenue rose 56%, organic revenue rose 51%, EPS more than doubled, and backlog reached $12.45B versus $6.89B a year earlier.
companyCandidates.risks: Project execution, labor availability, margin normalization, backlog burn timing, and limited explicit data-center revenue disclosure.
companyCandidates.potentialRead: Probably one of the best Step 6 businesses, but less AMD-like upside because the market already recognizes its data-center role and the company is larger and more mature.

companyCandidates.name: Everus Construction Group
companyCandidates.why: Newer public contractor with Electrical & Mechanical and Transmission & Distribution exposure. Q1 2026 revenue rose 25.4%, EPS rose 58.3%, and backlog reached $3.68B.
companyCandidates.risks: Limited public-company history, construction execution, cyclical demand, labor availability, and customer/project concentration.
companyCandidates.potentialRead: Interesting newer public contractor with enough electrical and T&D exposure to matter, but less proven disclosure history makes the signal lower confidence than IESC/FIX/STRL.

companyCandidates.name: EMCOR Group
companyCandidates.why: Large complex-project contractor for data-center electrical and mechanical work. Q1 2026 revenue rose 19.7%, diluted EPS rose 30.0%, remaining performance obligations reached $15.62B, and management raised 2026 guidance.
companyCandidates.risks: Less pure than specialist cooling/electrical names, fixed-price project risk, labor constraints, M&A integration, and margin normalization.
companyCandidates.potentialRead: Very investable quality, but more diversified and already institutional; the AI read-through is strong without the same step-change optionality as smaller specialists.

companyCandidates.name: Hubbell
companyCandidates.why: Direct Step 6 grid/electrical supplier across connectors, fittings, wire management, utility distribution, and data-center electrical infrastructure. Q1 2026 sales grew 11%, both segments grew double digits, and the pending NSI acquisition adds data-center/network-infrastructure products.
companyCandidates.risks: Broad industrial/utility mix, M&A leverage and integration, input costs, and utility capex timing.
companyCandidates.source: Hubbell Q1 2026 results / NSI acquisition, Apr 30-May 4 2026
companyCandidates.potentialRead: Good Step 6 compounder across grid and electrical products, strengthened by NSI, but the large diversified base and acquisition debt make it less AMD-like.

companyCandidates.name: Trane Technologies
companyCandidates.why: High-quality cooling platform with a broader HVAC base. Q1 2026 organic bookings rose 24%, Americas Commercial HVAC bookings rose about 40%, applied equipment bookings were up more than 160%, and backlog reached a record $10.7B.
companyCandidates.risks: Diversified HVAC dilutes AI sensitivity, acquisition integration, commercial HVAC cyclicality, and technology-transition risk.
companyCandidates.potentialRead: Excellent cooling platform and strong backlog, but HVAC diversification and mega-cap quality profile reduce the probability of an AMD-style rerating.

companyCandidates.name: Talen Energy
companyCandidates.why: Direct power-generation exposure to data centers through the Susquehanna nuclear relationship with Amazon, expanded to supply up to 1,920 MW through 2042.
companyCandidates.risks: FERC/regulatory complexity, nuclear outage/refueling risk, PJM power-price volatility, and leverage from growth deals.
companyCandidates.potentialRead: Strong nuclear-to-data-center narrative, but it is more exposed to regulation, PJM pricing, and contract structure than a direct equipment or cooling supplier.

companyCandidates.name: Generac
companyCandidates.why: Q1 2026 commercial and industrial sales rose about 28%, driven by global data-center customers, and the Enercon deal adds data-center power equipment depth. The AI angle still sits beside residential generator cyclicality.
companyCandidates.risks: Residential demand swings, hyperscaler approval timing, C&I margin mix, integration risk, and backup-power competition.
companyCandidates.potentialRead: The data-center generator angle is real and improving, but residential cyclicality keeps the stock from screening as a clean Step 6 AI infrastructure winner.

companyCandidates.name: NRG Energy
companyCandidates.why: The LS Power acquisition added 13 GW of quick-start gas generation and a 6 GW C&I virtual power plant platform. Direct, but more exposed to commodity power spreads than equipment suppliers.
companyCandidates.risks: Gas price and spark-spread exposure, carbon/regulatory pressure, LS Power integration, and data-center contract timing.
companyCandidates.source: NRG LS Power regulatory approval/close, Jan 2026
companyCandidates.potentialRead: Load-growth optionality is meaningful after LS Power, but equity upside depends heavily on power spreads, gas generation economics, and contract timing.

companyCandidates.name: Atkore
companyCandidates.why: Real Step 6 supplier for conduit, fittings, cable tray, prefab and modular electrical products, but Q2 FY2026 showed margin pressure, legal settlement expense, divestitures, and continued commodity/cyclical drag.
companyCandidates.risks: Pricing deflation, PVC/steel input cycles, litigation, nonresidential construction demand, and lower margins versus peak years.
companyCandidates.potentialRead: Could rebound if electrical-products demand tightens, but current fundamentals are dominated by margin pressure, settlements, and commodity product cycles rather than AI scarcity.

companyCandidates.name: American Electric Power
companyCandidates.why: Huge signed large-load signal from data centers and hyperscalers, with incremental load raised to 63 GW by 2030 and the five-year capital plan lifted to $78B. Still better treated as broader because equity returns depend on regulated utility rate-base mechanics.
companyCandidates.risks: Regulatory lag, customer cost allocation, financing needs, generation availability, and political pushback on data-center bills.
companyCandidates.potentialRead: Best evidence that Step 6 demand is real, but not the most AMD-like equity because regulated utility returns are steadier and capped even when load growth is huge.

companies.macroAngle: Architecture moat - if AI compute keeps growing, royalty pool grows with it regardless of which chip vendor wins.
companies.keyRisks: Trades at 110x fwd - 220% above semi industry median. Any guidance softness is brutal.

companies.macroAngle: Performance marketing budgets move toward systems that can prove ROI; AI bidding and targeting can compound if e-commerce expansion works.

health.balance: Debt present, but covered by high cash generation

companies.expectedMove: High beta; recent post-earnings moves have been double-digit
companies.keyRisks: Adtech privacy scrutiny, Apple/Google platform policy, regulatory headlines, competition, and valuation compression.

financials.source: StockAnalysis financials and subagent research, annual values in millions USD

dcf.note: DCF support depends on sustaining unusually high margins and avoiding platform or regulatory shocks.

companies.name: Tempus AI
companies.subTheme: AI Precision Medicine / Clinical Data Platform
companies.thesis: Tempus applies AI to precision medicine using multimodal clinical and molecular data, diagnostics, clinical decision support, trial matching, and pharma data products. Picked because healthcare is one of the largest potential AI workflow markets outside enterprise software.
companies.macroAngle: Healthcare AI adoption is tied to diagnostics volume, oncology decision support, pharma R&D productivity, and payer/provider pressure to personalize care.

health.balance: Cash present but net debt after acquisitions

companies.keyRisks: Cash burn, reimbursement pressure, acquisition integration, healthcare data/privacy rules, and dilution/leverage risk.

financials.source: StockAnalysis financials and subagent research, annual values in millions USD

dcf.note: Better suited to a path-to-FCF or revenue-multiple model until durable positive FCF is visible.

companies.name: SoundHound AI
companies.thesis: SoundHound provides voice and conversational AI for restaurants, autos, telecom, customer service, and enterprise agents. Picked as a high-risk pure-play on voice agents and call-center/order automation.
companies.macroAngle: Labor shortages and customer-service cost pressure can push enterprises toward voice agents if accuracy and integration quality improve.
companies.keyRisks: Still unprofitable, acquisition integration, customer concentration, hyperscaler speech competition, and dilution risk.

financials.source: StockAnalysis financials and subagent research, annual values in millions USD

dcf.note: Use a scenario model until margins and post-acquisition FCF normalize.

companies.name: C3.ai
companies.thesis: C3.ai is a pure-play enterprise AI application vendor for industrial, federal, healthcare, financial, and other large-enterprise use cases. Picked as a distressed/turnaround AI software read-through, not a quality compounder.
companies.macroAngle: If enterprises buy packaged AI applications instead of building everything on hyperscaler platforms, C3.ai has optionality.

health.balance: Large cash balance gives turnaround runway

companies.keyRisks: Revenue decline, leadership transition, restructuring execution, gross margin compression, deal timing, and hyperscaler/incumbent competition.

financials.source: StockAnalysis financials and subagent research, annual/TTM values in millions USD
financials.quarterlySource: Yahoo Finance quarterly statements via yfinance, values in millions USD

dcf.note: Cash runway and stabilization milestones matter more than DCF until revenue growth and margins recover.

companies.name: Astera Labs
companies.thesis: Astera Labs sells high-speed connectivity chips and software for cloud and AI infrastructure, including retimers, CXL/Ethernet connectivity, and rack-scale smart fabric products. Picked because AI clusters need faster, more reliable data movement, not only GPUs.
companies.macroAngle: As AI racks scale out, copper, optical, CXL, PCIe, and Ethernet connectivity can become bottlenecks. Astera is a direct rack-scale AI connectivity play.
companies.keyRisks: Very high valuation, customer concentration, short public history, AI networking standard shifts, and competition from larger chip vendors.

financials.source: StockAnalysis financials and company reporting, limited public history, values in millions USD

dcf.note: Short trading history and premium AI multiple make DCF highly sensitive to growth fade assumptions.

companies.name: Teradyne
companies.subTheme: AI Compute, Networking and Memory Test
companies.thesis: Teradyne is a semiconductor-test play on AI compute, HBM, and high-speed networking complexity. Picked because AI chips and memory devices require more intensive test coverage as packages become larger and more complex.
companies.macroAngle: More AI silicon complexity means higher test intensity per device, even when unit volumes are lumpy.
companies.keyRisks: Customer concentration, AI test pull-forward, semiconductor capex cyclicality, and valuation after a major AI re-rate.

financials.source: StockAnalysis financials and subagent research, annual values in millions USD
financials.quarterlySource: Yahoo Finance quarterly statements via yfinance, values in millions USD

dcf.note: Quality test business, but valuation requires sustained AI test share and cycle-normal demand.

companies.name: Monolithic Power Systems
companies.thesis: Monolithic Power Systems supplies high-performance power electronics used in servers, AI systems, memory, storage, and networking. Picked because denser AI racks need more efficient power conversion and thermal-aware power delivery.
companies.macroAngle: AI accelerator power draw keeps rising; power-management chips become more strategic as rack-level power density climbs.
companies.keyRisks: Very high valuation, inventory timing, customer/platform concentration, and competition in power modules.

financials.source: StockAnalysis financials and subagent research, annual values in millions USD
financials.quarterlySource: Monolithic Power Q1 2026 Form 10-Q, values in millions USD; FCF computed as operating cash flow less capex

dcf.note: DCF works for the business model, but the current valuation needs a long AI power runway.

companies.name: Fabrinet
companies.thesis: Fabrinet provides optical packaging and precision manufacturing services for advanced optical and electro-mechanical products. Picked because AI clusters are driving demand for optical modules, high-performance compute connectivity, DCI, and advanced packaging capacity.
companies.macroAngle: AI data centers need more optical links and manufacturing capacity as cluster bandwidth demand rises.
companies.keyRisks: Customer concentration, optical-cycle volatility, Thailand manufacturing exposure, and margin compression during capacity ramps.

financials.source: StockAnalysis financials and subagent research, annual values in millions USD
financials.quarterlySource: Fabrinet fiscal Q3 2026 results, values in millions USD; FCF is reported non-GAAP free cash flow

dcf.note: Useful, but working-capital and capex swings can distort near-term FCF.

companies.name: Onto Innovation
companies.thesis: Onto Innovation sells process-control, metrology, inspection, lithography, and analytics tools tied to advanced packaging and AI device manufacturing. Picked because HBM, 2.5D packaging, and heterogeneous integration raise yield-control requirements.
companies.macroAngle: AI advanced packaging increases the cost of defects, making inspection and metrology more valuable in the supply chain.
companies.keyRisks: Packaging capex timing, China/export controls, semiconductor equipment cyclicality, and integration risk.

financials.source: StockAnalysis financials and subagent research, annual values in millions USD

dcf.note: Strong balance sheet helps, but cycle-normal margins matter.

companies.name: Cohu
companies.thesis: Cohu supplies semiconductor test equipment, handlers, inspection, contactors, thermal subsystems, and data analytics. Picked as a smaller turnaround play on AI/HPC back-end test demand.
companies.macroAngle: AI processors, HBM, and high-power compute devices increase the need for back-end test, inspection, and thermal handling.
companies.keyRisks: Execution risk, still-negative GAAP margins, cyclical auto/industrial recovery, and lumpy AI test orders.

companies.name: Eaton
companies.subTheme: Data Center Power Distribution + Liquid Cooling
companies.thesis: Eaton is a grid-to-chip supplier for data centers: switchgear, UPS/power quality, electrical distribution, and liquid-cooling capabilities after Boyd Thermal. Picked because AI factories need power reliability before GPUs can be deployed.
companies.macroAngle: AI capex raises electrical load density, increasing demand for power distribution, utility interconnects, and cooling infrastructure.
companies.keyRisks: Rich valuation, data-center order timing, Boyd Thermal integration, tariffs, and input-cost pressure.

financials.source: StockAnalysis financials and subagent research, annual values in millions USD
financials.quarterlySource: Eaton Q1 2026 results, values in millions USD; FCF reported by company

companies.name: Quanta Services
companies.thesis: Quanta builds and services electric transmission, distribution, substations, and large-load interconnects. Picked because AI data centers require grid construction, transformer/substation work, and faster power-delivery execution.
companies.macroAngle: The AI power bottleneck is partly a construction bottleneck; Quanta benefits when utilities and hyperscalers accelerate grid work.
companies.keyRisks: Labor availability, project execution, weather, utility capex cycles, political risk, and premium valuation.

financials.source: StockAnalysis financials and subagent research, annual values in millions USD
financials.quarterlySource: Yahoo Finance quarterly statements via yfinance, values in millions USD

dcf.note: Backlog gives visibility, but low margins and working-capital swings make DCF sensitive.

companies.name: Carrier Global
companies.thesis: Carrier supplies commercial HVAC, chillers, building controls, aftermarket service, and data-center cooling solutions. Picked because AI clusters raise thermal density and Carrier reported a large data-center order surge.
companies.macroAngle: AI racks need reliable heat removal; cooling order commentary is increasingly important for the physical AI buildout.

health.balance: Debt elevated but supported by FCF

companies.keyRisks: Cyclical HVAC demand, debt load, margin pressure, and competition in data-center cooling.

financials.source: StockAnalysis financials and subagent research, annual values in millions USD
financials.quarterlySource: Yahoo Finance quarterly statements via yfinance, values in millions USD

companies.name: nVent Electric
companies.thesis: nVent sells electrical connection and protection products, enclosures, bus systems, cable management, and thermal infrastructure for mission-critical applications including data centers. Picked as a smaller electrical-infrastructure beneficiary of AI rack growth.
companies.macroAngle: AI racks require higher-density power connection, protection, enclosures, bus systems, and thermal management.
companies.keyRisks: Data-center order lumpiness, tariff/input costs, acquisition integration, and margin dilution from capacity expansion.

financials.source: StockAnalysis financials and subagent research, annual values in millions USD

companies.name: GE Vernova
companies.subTheme: Power Generation, Grid Equipment and Electrification
companies.thesis: GE Vernova sells power generation, grid, and electrification equipment; data-center demand is pulling forward orders for power and grid infrastructure. Picked because AI power demand can support gas turbines, transformers, substations, and grid modernization.
companies.macroAngle: AI data centers need new electricity supply and grid equipment, turning power infrastructure into a direct AI capacity constraint.
companies.keyRisks: Valuation, gas-turbine capacity constraints, wind segment drag, tariffs, project execution, and power policy changes.

companies.name: Vishay Intertechnology
companies.thesis: Vishay is a broad discrete semiconductor and passive-components supplier with an emerging AI infrastructure angle: power MOSFETs, diodes, resistors, inductors, capacitors, and thin-film substrates that can show up in AI server power chains, optical transceivers, and advanced packaging. Added as a lower-quality AI component/supply-chain watch because management explicitly called out AI-related power applications, but the stock is still primarily a cyclical components business.
companies.macroAngle: AI racks raise power density, thermal stress, and high-speed optical packaging requirements. Vishay benefits if AI server and optical-module demand broadens into commodity power/passive components, but it is much less direct than MPWR, FN, or semicap equipment names.

Upside needs stronger order conversion, improved Newport drag, and evidence that AI-related power/optical demand can lift margins rather than only revenue.
companies.keyRisks: Weak direct AI purity, negative FY25 free cash flow, very low operating margin, debt above cash, cyclical industrial/auto exposure, and analyst target materially below the current price after the stock's sharp rally.

broaderWatchlist.name: Apple
broaderWatchlist.thesis: Apple is here as a quality compounder watch, not an AI-pure-play. The reason to track it is simple: huge installed base, services margin, buybacks, and very large free cash flow. The current debate is whether iPhone/Mac demand and Apple Intelligence can restart growth enough to justify the premium multiple.
broaderWatchlist.macroAngle: Broader watch angle: consumer hardware demand, services durability, memory cost pressure, and whether Apple can close the perceived AI gap without hurting margins.
broaderWatchlist.keyRisks: Valuation is already rich for a slower-growth mega-cap. China demand, App Store regulation, memory/component inflation, and delayed AI execution can pressure both revenue growth and the multiple.

financials.source: StockAnalysis financials, annual values in millions USD
financials.quarterlySource: Apple FY2026 Q2 Form 10-Q, values in millions USD; cash-flow fields derived from six-month less Q1; FCF computed as operating cash flow less capex

dcf.note: AAPL is one of the cleaner DCF names because cash flow, buybacks, and margins are mature and visible.

broaderWatchlist.name: Tesla
broaderWatchlist.thesis: Tesla is a high-beta story stock. The dashboard should track whether the core EV business is stabilizing while the market keeps paying for robotaxi, autonomy, energy storage, and robotics optionality. It is not cheap on current earnings, so delivery growth and margin recovery matter a lot.
broaderWatchlist.macroAngle: Broader watch angle: EV demand, price cuts, battery costs, autonomous driving regulation, and whether non-car businesses can support the valuation.
broaderWatchlist.keyRisks: Current earnings do not support the full valuation without major future optionality. EV competition, margin compression, regulatory risk, execution delays, and CEO/key-person risk can move the stock sharply.

financials.source: StockAnalysis financials, annual values in millions USD
financials.quarterlySource: Yahoo Finance quarterly statements via yfinance, values in millions USD

dcf.note: TSLA DCF is highly assumption-driven because much of the market value depends on future optionality, not current cash flow.

broaderWatchlist.name: Grab Holdings
broaderWatchlist.thesis: Grab is a regional growth and profitability watch. The reason to track it is whether mobility, delivery, fintech, and advertising can keep compounding while the company turns accounting profit into durable free cash flow. The balance sheet gives it room, but cash conversion is the key proof point.
broaderWatchlist.macroAngle: Broader watch angle: Southeast Asia consumer demand, take-rate expansion, fintech losses, competition intensity, and whether incentives/subsidies stay disciplined.
broaderWatchlist.keyRisks: Competition in delivery and ride-hailing can force subsidies back up. Fintech credit risk, regulation, FX moves, and weak free cash flow can keep the stock volatile even if revenue grows.

financials.source: StockAnalysis financials, annual values in millions USD
financials.quarterlySource: Grab Q1 2026 results, values in millions USD; EBITDA and FCF are adjusted measures

dcf.note: GRAB is becoming profitable, but the model is still sensitive to cash conversion and reinvestment assumptions.

broaderWatchlist.name: Unity Software
broaderWatchlist.thesis: Unity is a turnaround watch. The core question is whether the company can rebuild developer trust, stabilize Create, and make the ad/monetization business grow again after restructuring. It has real platform value, but the proof needs to show up in revenue quality and free cash flow.
broaderWatchlist.macroAngle: Broader watch angle: gaming demand, AI-generated content risk, ad-tech recovery, cost discipline, and whether Unity can grow without damaging its developer ecosystem.
broaderWatchlist.keyRisks: Turnaround execution is the risk. Revenue can remain choppy, AI tools may pressure game-engine value, and past pricing/trust issues can slow adoption. The company still reports negative GAAP earnings.

financials.source: StockAnalysis financials, annual values in millions USD

dcf.note: Unity has cash-flow potential, but a DCF depends heavily on margin recovery and sustained product trust.

broaderWatchlist.name: Alibaba Group
broaderWatchlist.thesis: Alibaba is a broader platform watch, not an AI pure-play. The core business is still China commerce, international e-commerce, local services, logistics, and cloud. The AI angle is real through Alibaba Cloud and Qwen, but the stock will still be driven by China consumer demand, competitive intensity, cloud growth, and whether AI spending converts into profitable revenue.
broaderWatchlist.macroAngle: Broader watch angle: China consumer recovery, cloud AI adoption, Qwen/model monetization, US-China restrictions, ADR sentiment, and whether higher AI infrastructure capex becomes durable cloud profit rather than just lower near-term free cash flow.
broaderWatchlist.keyRisks: China macro weakness, e-commerce and local-services price competition, regulatory/geopolitical risk, ADR sentiment, export controls, and heavy AI/cloud capex can all pressure margins and free cash flow.

financials.source: StockAnalysis financials, annual values converted from CNY to approximate millions USD

dcf.note: Alibaba generates real cash flow, but China macro risk, ADR/geopolitical risk, and AI cloud capex make the DCF more fragile than mature US mega-cap software names.

broaderWatchlist.name: Uber Technologies
broaderWatchlist.thesis: Uber is a broader platform watch, not an AI pure-play. The business now has real scale, margin expansion, and strong free cash flow across mobility and delivery. The key debate is whether autonomous vehicle fleets become a threat that bypasses Uber, or a supply layer that uses Uber as the demand aggregator.
broaderWatchlist.macroAngle: Broader watch angle: consumer mobility demand, delivery take-rate, driver supply, buyback pace, and whether AV partners use Uber distribution instead of competing directly.

health.balance: $7.6B unrestricted cash and short-term investments; current ratio 1.14

broaderWatchlist.keyRisks: Q1 earnings are due May 6, 2026 before market open. AV disruption from Waymo, Tesla, or fleet partners, driver classification/regulatory pressure, delivery competition, and weaker profit guidance can all compress the multiple.
